intro.text: This is Andaman and Nicobar, a long line of islands out in the sea, a very long way from the rest of India. It is more than a thousand kilometres of open water from Chennai to here. There are eight hundred and thirty-six islands, and only thirty-one of them have anybody living on them at all. The main town is called Sri Vijaya Puram. It used to be called Port Blair.

animal.text: The dugong is the animal of these islands. He is as long as a car, he lives in the sea, and all he eats is grass off the sea floor. People call him the sea cow.

food.text: A thousand years ago somebody wrote these islands down as Coconut Island. Coconut trees still grow all along the shore, and the boats still come in loaded with fish.

festival.text: Nearly everybody here came from somewhere else in India: from Bengal, from Tamil Nadu, from Kerala. Each family brought its own festivals, so all of those happen here.

hello.text: People here say Namaste in Hindi. But you will hear hello in Bengali too, and in Tamil, and in Telugu, because the families here came from all those places.

line.text: White sand, water so clear and so blue that it looks like a swimming pool, and thick forest coming right down to the top of the beach. You have to come here on a boat. The waves are gentle, so you can go in.

This island is a volcano, and it is the only one in the whole country that is still awake. It sits out in the sea by itself. Nobody lives on it, only a few wild goats, and it has boiled over more than ten times.

Water drips through the roof of these caves, and every single drop leaves a speck of stone behind it. Thousands of years of dripping, and now the rock hangs down off the ceiling in long shapes, like candles that have melted.

People built a whole little town on this island once, with a bakery and a church and a swimming pool, and then they went away and left it. The ruins are still standing among the palm trees, and spotted deer wander about in them.

This little orange fish lives inside a sea anemone, which has soft waving arms that sting. They would sting anything else that came near. The fish has a slippery coat that stops them, so it sleeps in there at night and nothing can get at it.
